children: Swedish consumer prices, measured with a fixed interest rate (CPIF), were up 0.7% year-on-year in August, a flash estimate released by the statistics office showed on Monday.
Analysts had forecast headline CPIF inflation of 1.0%, according to a Reuters poll.
Stripped of volatile energy prices, a measure watched closely by the central bank, the pace of inflation eased marginally to 0.5% compared to the same month a year earlier.

The Riksbank has been in wait-and-see mode since cutting the policy rate by a quarter percentage point in September last year, waiting for clearer signals about the direction of inflation and the economy.
Inflation has gradually picked up during the summer, when the effects of temporary tax cuts are excluded, while the domestic economy has improved and the crown currency weakened.
Many analysts now see a hike before year-end.
Inflation, however, remains a puzzle and Riksbank Governor Erik Thedeen said last week the risk-picture was not clear cut.
